newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Daiwa Europe sees Slovenian SBI above 2,000.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa Europe sees Slovenian SBI above 2,000.

text.p: The blue-chip SBI index could hit 2,000 points in the next few days, following a decision by Slovenia's central bank to relax rules for long-term foreign investors, brokers Daiwa Europe said on Tuesday.
The SBI index ended at 1,396.7 on Tuesday, down 3.30 percent or 47.62 points on what traders said was profit-taking from last week's gains. The index has risen 15.6 percent in the past week.

"However, this is only the beginning of what could be a sustained advance, since the general quality and growth potential of Slovenian companies is very good. This could carry the SBI index to a level above 2,000," said Daiwa Europe in a statement.
Daiwa added that the softening of the central bank's stance could be the first step of a phased normalisation, but noted that the current situation for foreign investors still needed improving.
"While the central bank has made equity trading manageable for foreigners, conditions are still far from ideal and can hardly be described as 'open'," the statement said.

Foreign investors withdrew in February when the central bank blocked foreign investment by ordering foreign buyers to open special custody accounts at high interest rates at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks.
Since then the SBI index tumbled over 20 percent while average daily volumes fell by over 80 percent.
Two weeks ago the central bank eased its stance on foreign investment with a ruling that funds paid into fiduciary accounts for a seven-year purchase should not be considered a foreign liability.

Banks welcomed the decision, which they said would enable them to reduce the costs of fiduciary accounts significantly. They had estimated the cost of the accounts at an average of 12 percent of the amount handled. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
